summary: A cognitive taxonomy can add boundaries and failure modes without improving task performance.

points.text: Real records cross categories: a correction learned during an incident is simultaneously episodic evidence, semantic knowledge, and a candidate procedure. Forced single-tier classification can discard important relationships.
Promotion and consolidation are themselves model judgments. A mistaken summary can transform a local episode into an apparently authoritative fact or procedure.
Multiple stores raise latency, operational cost, access-control complexity, and consistency risk. A small application may perform better with one typed store and filtered views.
Retrieval from several tiers can overfill context and create conflicts about precedence. Without explicit resolution policy, more organized storage produces less predictable behavior.
